revision.text:
'''酒見神社'''（さかみじんじゃ）は、[[愛知県]][[一宮市]]にある[[神社]]である。
[[延喜式]]神名帳に記載がある神社（式内社）であり、[[元伊勢]]の一つ。[[倭姫命]]の滞在地である。[[尾張国]]中嶋宮。
社殿は北向きとなっている。これは[[伊勢神宮]]へ向かって崇拝する為であるという。また、本殿の裏にある倭姫社は、壁が無い吹き抜け構造の社殿である。
酒との関わりが深い神社であり、酒の神である、酒弥豆男神、酒弥豆女神を祀る。境内には[[神酒|黒酒、白酒]]を納めたといわれる大甕（[[鎌倉時代]]作という）がある。
==祭神== *[[天照皇大御神]] *[[倭姫命]] *[[酒弥豆男神]] *[[酒弥豆女神]]
== 沿革 == [[垂仁天皇]]14年、[[美濃国]]伊久良河宮（現[[岐阜県]][[瑞穂市]]居倉[[天神神社 (瑞穂市)|天神神社]]と伝えられる）から倭姫命がこの地を訪れ、滞在したさい、地元の人々が建てたのが始まりという。社伝によれば、その時の社殿は全て丸い柱で造られ、草葺きの屋根で吹き抜けであったという。
[[斉衡]]3年（[[856年]]）、[[文徳天皇]]の勅命により伊勢神宮から、大邑刃自、小邑刃自の2名の酒造師がこの地に派遣され、伊勢神宮にお供えする御神酒を造ったと伝えられる。このことから、[[清酒]]の醸造が最初に行われた所といわれている。
== 所在地 == *愛知県一宮市今伊勢町本神戸字宮山1476
== 交通アクセス == *[[東海道本線]][[尾張一宮駅]]、[[名古屋鉄道]][[名鉄名古屋本線|名古屋本線]][[名鉄尾西線|尾西線]][[名鉄一宮駅]]より徒歩20分（約1.5km）。 *[[i-バス]]（一宮市循環バス）、酒見神社前バス停よりすぐ。 *[[愛知県道190号名古屋一宮線]]酒見神社前交差点よりすぐ。
[[Category:愛知県の神社|さかみしんしや]] [[Category:一宮市|さかみしんしや]] {{shinto-stub}}

{{神社| 名称=酒見神社| 所在地=愛知県一宮市今伊勢町本神戸字宮山1476| 位置={{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|35|18|56|N|136|47|42|E|scale:30000}}| 祭神=天照皇大御神
酒弥豆男神
酒弥豆女神| 社格=式内社（小）・郷社| 創建=[[垂仁天皇]]14年| 例祭=[[4月16日]]}} '''酒見神社'''（さかみじんじゃ）は、[[愛知県]][[一宮市]]にある[[神社]]である。[[式内社]]で、旧[[社格]]は[[郷社]]。[[倭姫命]]が滞在した「中嶋宮」の跡とされ、[[元伊勢]]の一つとなっている。 [[天照大神|天照皇大御神]]のほか、酒造の神である酒弥豆男神・酒弥豆女神を祀る。本殿の裏に倭姫社があり、倭姫命が祀られている。 ==歴史== 天照大神の御霊代を祀る地を求めて旅をしていた倭姫命は、[[垂仁天皇]]14年、[[美濃国]]伊久良河宮（現[[岐阜県]][[瑞穂市]]居倉[[天神神社 (瑞穂市)|天神神社]]と伝えられる）から尾張の神戸であった当地しばらく滞在し、神体を宮山に祀った。その後、地元の人々によって社殿が作られたのが当社の始まりであると伝える。社伝によれば、その時の社殿は全て丸い柱で造られ、草葺きの屋根で吹き抜けであったという。 [[斉衡]]3年（[[856年]]）、[[文徳天皇]]の勅命により[[伊勢神宮]]から、大邑刃自・小邑刃自の2名の酒造師がこの地に派遣され、伊勢神宮にお供えする御神酒を造ったと伝えられる。このことから、[[清酒]]の醸造が最初に行われた所といわれている。「酒見」の社名もこれに因むものである。 ==境内== 社殿は北向きとなっており、伊勢神宮のある南の方向に向かって拝礼することになる。また、本殿の裏にある倭姫社は、壁が無い吹き抜け構造の社殿である。 [[神酒|黒酒、白酒]]を納めたといわれる大甕（[[鎌倉時代]]作という）が社殿のそばにあり、社殿の前には酒を造るのに用いたという酒槽石がある。 == 交通アクセス == *[[東海道本線]][[尾張一宮駅]]、[[名古屋鉄道]][[名鉄名古屋本線|名古屋本線]][[名鉄尾西線|尾西線]][[名鉄一宮駅]]より徒歩20分（約1.5km）。 *[[i-バス]]（一宮市循環バス）、酒見神社前バス停よりすぐ。 *[[愛知県道190号名古屋一宮線]]酒見神社前交差点よりすぐ。 ==外部リンク== *[http://www.geocities.jp/engishiki01/owari/bun/ow100219-01.html ]（延喜式神社の調査） {{DEFAULTSORT:さかみしんしや}} [[Category:愛知県の神社]] [[Category:式内小社]] [[Category:郷社]] [[Category:一宮市]] {{shinto-stub}}

酒弥豆女神| 社格=式内社（小）・郷社| 創建=[[垂仁天皇]]14年| 例祭=[[4月16日]]}} '''酒見神社'''（さかみじんじゃ）は、[[愛知県]][[一宮市]]にある[[神社]]である。[[式内社]]で、旧[[社格]]は[[郷社]]。[[倭姫命]]が滞在した「中嶋宮」の跡とされ、[[元伊勢]]の一つとなっている。 [[天照大神|天照皇大御神]]のほか、酒造の神である酒弥豆男神・酒弥豆女神を祀る。本殿の裏に倭姫社があり、倭姫命が祀られている。 ==歴史== 天照大神の御霊代を祀る地を求めて旅をしていた倭姫命は、[[垂仁天皇]]14年、[[美濃国]]伊久良河宮（現[[岐阜県]][[瑞穂市]]居倉[[天神神社 (瑞穂市)|天神神社]]と伝えられる）から尾張の神戸であった当地しばらく滞在し、神体を宮山に祀った。その後、地元の人々によって社殿が作られたのが当社の始まりであると伝える。社伝によれば、その時の社殿は全て丸い柱で造られ、草葺きの屋根で吹き抜けであったという。 [[斉衡]]3年（[[856年]]）、[[文徳天皇]]の勅命により[[伊勢神宮]]から、大邑刃自・小邑刃自の2名の酒造師がこの地に派遣され、伊勢神宮に[[供物|お供え]]する御神酒を造ったと伝えられる。このことから、[[清酒]]の醸造が最初に行われた所といわれている。「酒見」の社名もこれに因むものである。 ==境内== 社殿は北向きとなっており、伊勢神宮のある南の方向に向かって拝礼することになる。また、本殿の裏にある倭姫社は、壁が無い吹き抜け構造の社殿である。 [[神酒|黒酒、白酒]]を納めたといわれる大甕（[[鎌倉時代]]作という）が社殿のそばにあり、社殿の前には酒を造るのに用いたという酒槽石がある。 ==都市伝説== 　この神社には地元に伝わる珍しい都市伝説が残る。 一つ目は、社殿は北向きいう珍しい建物の為、戦後は「逆見（さかみ）神社とも呼ばれた事。二つ目は住所が（今）伊勢町（本）神戸と伊勢神宮にかなり強い対抗心の高い住所名の為、この神社の神は伊勢に対抗して立てられたいう話が残っている。 == 交通アクセス == *[[東海道本線]][[尾張一宮駅]]、[[名古屋鉄道]][[名鉄名古屋本線|名古屋本線]][[名鉄尾西線|尾西線]][[名鉄一宮駅]]より徒歩20分（約1.5km）。 *[[i-バス]]（一宮市循環バス）、酒見神社前バス停よりすぐ。 *[[愛知県道190号名古屋一宮線]]酒見神社前交差点よりすぐ。 ==外部リンク== *[http://www.geocities.jp/engishiki01/owari/bun/ow100219-01.html ]（延喜式神社の調査） {{DEFAULTSORT:さかみしんしや}} [[Category:一宮市の神社]] [[Category:式内小社]] [[Category:郷社]] {{shinto-stub}}

酒弥豆女神| 社格=式内社（小）・郷社| 創建=[[垂仁天皇]]14年| 例祭=[[4月16日]]}} '''酒見神社'''（さかみじんじゃ）は、[[愛知県]][[一宮市]]にある[[神社]]である。[[式内社]]で、旧[[社格]]は[[郷社]]。[[倭姫命]]が滞在した「中嶋宮」の跡とされ、[[元伊勢]]の一つとなっている。 [[天照大神|天照皇大御神]]のほか、酒造の神である酒弥豆男神・酒弥豆女神を祀る。本殿の裏に倭姫社があり、倭姫命が祀られている。 ==歴史== 天照大神の御霊代を祀る地を求めて旅をしていた倭姫命は、[[垂仁天皇]]14年、[[美濃国]]伊久良河宮（現[[岐阜県]][[瑞穂市]]居倉[[天神神社 (瑞穂市)|天神神社]]と伝えられる）から尾張の神戸であった当地しばらく滞在し、神体を宮山に祀った。その後、地元の人々によって社殿が作られたのが当社の始まりであると伝える。社伝によれば、その時の社殿は全て丸い柱で造られ、草葺きの屋根で吹き抜けであったという。 [[斉衡]]3年（[[856年]]）、[[文徳天皇]]の勅命により[[伊勢神宮]]から、大邑刃自・小邑刃自の2名の酒造師がこの地に派遣され、伊勢神宮に[[供物|お供え]]する御神酒を造ったと伝えられる。このことから、[[清酒]]の醸造が最初に行われた所といわれている。「酒見」の社名もこれに因むものである。 ==境内== 社殿は北向きとなっており、伊勢神宮のある南の方向に向かって拝礼することになる。また、本殿の裏にある倭姫社は、壁が無い吹き抜け構造の社殿である。 [[神酒|黒酒、白酒]]を納めたといわれる大甕（[[鎌倉時代]]作という）が社殿のそばにあり、社殿の前には酒を造るのに用いたという酒槽石がある。 ==都市伝説== 　この神社には地元に伝わる珍しい都市伝説が残る。 一つ目は、社殿は北向きいう珍しい建物の為、戦後は「逆見（さかみ）神社」とも呼ばれた事。二つ目は住所が（今）伊勢町（本）神戸と伊勢神宮にかなり強い対抗心の高い住所名の為、この神社の神は伊勢に対抗して立てられたいう話が残っている。 == 交通アクセス == *[[東海道本線]][[尾張一宮駅]]、[[名古屋鉄道]][[名鉄名古屋本線|名古屋本線]][[名鉄尾西線|尾西線]][[名鉄一宮駅]]より徒歩20分（約1.5km）。 *[[i-バス]]（一宮市循環バス）、酒見神社前バス停よりすぐ。 *[[愛知県道190号名古屋一宮線]]酒見神社前交差点よりすぐ。 ==外部リンク== *[http://www.geocities.jp/engishiki01/owari/bun/ow100219-01.html ]（延喜式神社の調査） {{DEFAULTSORT:さかみしんしや}} [[Category:一宮市の神社]] [[Category:式内小社]] [[Category:愛知県の旧郷社]] {{shinto-stub}}

酒弥豆女神| 社格=式内社（小）・郷社| 創建=[[垂仁天皇]]14年| 例祭=[[4月16日]]}} '''酒見神社'''（さかみじんじゃ）は、[[愛知県]][[一宮市]]にある[[神社]]である。[[式内社]]で、旧[[社格]]は[[郷社]]。[[倭姫命]]が滞在した「中嶋宮」の跡とされ、[[元伊勢]]の一つとなっている。 [[天照大神|天照皇大御神]]のほか、酒造の神である酒弥豆男神・酒弥豆女神を祀る。本殿の裏に倭姫社があり、倭姫命が祀られている。 ==歴史== 天照大神の御霊代を祀る地を求めて旅をしていた倭姫命は、[[垂仁天皇]]14年、[[美濃国]]伊久良河宮（現[[岐阜県]][[瑞穂市]]居倉[[天神神社 (瑞穂市)|天神神社]]と伝えられる）から尾張の神戸であった当地しばらく滞在し、神体を宮山に祀った。その後、地元の人々によって社殿が作られたのが当社の始まりであると伝える。社伝によれば、その時の社殿は全て丸い柱で造られ、草葺きの屋根で吹き抜けであったという。 [[斉衡]]3年（[[856年]]）、[[文徳天皇]]の勅命により[[伊勢神宮]]から、大邑刃自・小邑刃自の2名の酒造師がこの地に派遣され、伊勢神宮に[[供物|お供え]]する御神酒を造ったと伝えられる。このことから、[[清酒]]の醸造が最初に行われた所といわれている。「酒見」の社名もこれに因むものである。 ==境内== 社殿は北向きとなっており、伊勢神宮のある南の方向に向かって拝礼することになる。また、本殿の裏にある倭姫社は、壁が無い吹き抜け構造の社殿である。 [[神酒|黒酒、白酒]]を納めたといわれる大甕（[[鎌倉時代]]作という）が社殿のそばにあり、社殿の前には酒を造るのに用いたという酒槽石がある。 ==都市伝説== この神社には地元に伝わる珍しい都市伝説が残る。 一つ目は、社殿は北向きいう珍しい建物の為、戦後は「逆見（さかみ）神社」とも呼ばれた事。二つ目は住所が（今）伊勢町（本）神戸と伊勢神宮にかなり強い対抗心の高い住所名の為、この神社の神は伊勢に対抗して立てられたいう話が残っている。 == 交通アクセス == *[[東海道本線]][[尾張一宮駅]]、[[名古屋鉄道]][[名鉄名古屋本線|名古屋本線]][[名鉄尾西線|尾西線]][[名鉄一宮駅]]より徒歩20分（約1.5km）。 *[[i-バス]]（一宮市循環バス）、酒見神社前バス停よりすぐ。 *[[愛知県道190号名古屋一宮線]]酒見神社前交差点よりすぐ。 {{shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:さかみしんしや}} [[Category:一宮市の神社]] [[Category:尾張国の式内社]] [[Category:愛知県の旧郷社]]

More sources to add{{Cite book |last=Kidder |first=J. Edward |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA201 |title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology |date=2007-02-28 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Stalker |first=Nancy K. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA62 |title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan |date=2007-10-31 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Authors |first=Various |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XEIiEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA534 |title=RLE: Japan Mini-Set F: Philosophy and Religion (4 vols) |date=2021-03-18 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-136-90356-4 |language=en}}{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nPaezHFlfNQC&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PT107 |title=Where the Trees Grow Thick |isbn=978-0-595-28240-1 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last1=Göttler |first1=Christine |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uyk_DwAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA437 |title=The Nomadic Object: The Challenge of World for Early Modern Religious Art |last2=Mochizuki |first2=Mia |date=2017-11-06 |publisher=BRILL |isbn=978-90-04-35450-0 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Picken |first=Stuart D. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xlG3F6gSm9UC&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA232 |title=Historical Dictionary of Shinto |date=2010-12-28 |publisher=Scarecrow Press |isbn=978-0-8108-7372-8 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Dougill |first=John |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-H_cEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PT204 |title=Off the Beaten Tracks in Japan: A Journey by Train from Hokkaido to Kyushu |date=2023-11-07 |publisher=Stone Bridge Press, Inc. |isbn=978-1-61172-963-4 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Ponsonby-Fane |first=R. A. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BY23AwAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA555 |title=Studies In Shinto & Shrines |date=2014-06-03 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-136-89294-3 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Ponsonby-Fane |first=R. A. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BY23AwAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA555 |title=Studies In Shinto & Shrines |date=2014-06-03 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-136-89294-3 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Army |first=United States Department of the |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PvgsAAAAIAAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=RA3-PA147 |title=Pamphlet - Dept. of the Army |date=1945 |publisher=Headquarters, Department of the Army. |language=en}}{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=MVHoAAAAMAAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA147 |title=Department of the Army Pamphlet |date=1945 |publisher=The Department |language=en}} ==Overview== {{Citation needed|date=October 27, 2014}} {{Infobox religious building | name = '''Sakami Jinja''' (酒見神社) | image = File:Sakami-jinja Shrine in Ichinomiya B.jpg | location = 1476 Miyayama, Moto-Kōbe aza, Imaisechō, [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]], [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35.315556|N|136.795|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]]
{{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
{{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor) · {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | founded = 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | festival = April 16 | prefecture= {{ill|Imaise-chō Hon-kambe|qid=Q127432721}} }} '''Sakami Jinja''' (酒見神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]], [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and its former rank was {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. It stands on the site of the Nakashima-no-Miya where [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] once stayed, and is regarded as one of the original {{ill|Moto Ise Shrines|de|Moto-Ise-Schreine|ja|元伊勢|zh|元伊势|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto Ise Shrines|qq=|1=Moto Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11387775}}. In addition to [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the shrine also enshrines {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the ancestor of sake brewers, and {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, dedicated to [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]]. == History == When Princess Yamatohime, seeking a site to enshrine the spirit of Amaterasu Ōmikami, traveled to this area in the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] from the Ikuragawa-no-Miya in Mino Province (now [[:en:Mizuho, Gifu|Mizuho]]), she stayed at what was then known as Kōbe in Owari and enshrined the sacred object on Mount Miya. The shrine was later built by the local people. According to tradition, the original building had round pillars, a thatched roof, and an open interior. In the 3rd year of the [[:en:Saikō|Shōhei era]] (856), by imperial order of [[:en:Emperor Montoku|Emperor Montoku]], two sake brewers—Ōmura no Haji and Komura no Haji—were dispatched from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] to produce the sacred sake offerings. This event marks the site as the birthplace of sake brewing, from which the shrine’s name “Sakami” is derived. == Grounds == The shrine buildings face north, so worshippers pray facing south toward the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]]. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, featuring an open-walled design. A large jar (dated to the Kamakura period) said to have stored {{ill|kurozake|de|Schwarzsake|ja|黒酒|zh|黑酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kurozake|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神酒|1=miki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3313722}} and {{ill|shirozake|de|Weißsake|ja|白酒|zh|白酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shirozake|qq=|1=shiroki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580387}} stands beside the hall, and in front lies a stone trough once used in sake production. == Local Legends == Two unusual local legends surround this shrine. First, because the shrine faces north, it was nicknamed “Reverse Sakami Jinja” (逆見神社) after World War II. Second, the address Imaisechō Motokōbe suggests rivalry with Ise, leading to the tale that the shrine was established in competition with the Ise Grand Shrine. == Access == * 20-minute walk (about 1.5 km) from [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|Owari Ichinomiya Station]] on the [[:en:Tōkaidō Main Line|Tōkaidō Main Line]] and [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Ichinomiya Station]] on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|de|Meitetsu-Nagoya-Hauptlinie|ja|名古屋鉄道 名鉄名古屋本線|zh|名古屋铁道 名鉄名古屋本线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the [[:en:Meitetsu Bisai Line|Bisai Line]]. * {{ill|i-Bus|de|i-Bus|ja|i-バス|zh|i公交|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/i-Bus|qq=|1=I-Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11223722}} circular bus to the Sakami Jinja-mae stop. * Immediately at the Sakami Jinja-mae intersection on {{ill|Aichi Prefectural Route 190|de|Aichi-Präfekturstraße 190|ja|愛知県道190号名古屋一宮線|zh|爱知县道190号名古宮线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefectural Route 190|qq=|1=Aichi Prefectural Road Route 190|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11494441}}. {{shinto-stub}} ==List of Motoise Shrines== {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; white-space:nowrap; font-size:85%" |- ! {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor) · {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | founded = 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | festival = April 16 | prefecture= {{ill|Imaise-chō Hon-kambe|qid=Q127432721}} }} '''Sakami Jinja''' (酒見神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]], [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and its former rank was {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. It stands on the site of the Nakashima-no-Miya where [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] once stayed, and is regarded as one of the original {{ill|Moto Ise Shrines|de|Moto-Ise-Schreine|ja|元伊勢|zh|元伊势|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto Ise Shrines|qq=|1=Moto Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11387775}}. In addition to [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the shrine also enshrines {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the ancestor of sake brewers, and {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, dedicated to [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]]. == History == When Princess Yamatohime, seeking a site to enshrine the spirit of Amaterasu Ōmikami, traveled to this area in the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] from the Ikuragawa-no-Miya in Mino Province (now [[:en:Mizuho, Gifu|Mizuho]]), she stayed at what was then known as Kōbe in Owari and enshrined the sacred object on Mount Miya. The shrine was later built by the local people. According to tradition, the original building had round pillars, a thatched roof, and an open interior. In the 3rd year of the [[:en:Saikō|Shōhei era]] (856), by imperial order of [[:en:Emperor Montoku|Emperor Montoku]], two sake brewers—Ōmura no Haji and Komura no Haji—were dispatched from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] to produce the sacred sake offerings. This event marks the site as the birthplace of sake brewing, from which the shrine’s name “Sakami” is derived. == Grounds == The shrine buildings face north, so worshippers pray facing south toward the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]]. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, featuring an open-walled design. A large jar (dated to the Kamakura period) said to have stored {{ill|kurozake|de|Schwarzsake|ja|黒酒|zh|黑酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kurozake|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神酒|1=miki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3313722}} and {{ill|shirozake|de|Weißsake|ja|白酒|zh|白酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shirozake|qq=|1=shiroki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580387}} stands beside the hall, and in front lies a stone trough once used in sake production. == Local Legends == Two unusual local legends surround this shrine. First, because the shrine faces north, it was nicknamed “Reverse Sakami Jinja” (逆見神社) after World War II. Second, the address Imaisechō Motokōbe suggests rivalry with Ise, leading to the tale that the shrine was established in competition with the Ise Grand Shrine. == Access == * 20-minute walk (about 1.5 km) from [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|Owari Ichinomiya Station]] on the [[:en:Tōkaidō Main Line|Tōkaidō Main Line]] and [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Ichinomiya Station]] on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|de|Meitetsu-Nagoya-Hauptlinie|ja|名古屋鉄道 名鉄名古屋本線|zh|名古屋铁道 名鉄名古屋本线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the [[:en:Meitetsu Bisai Line|Bisai Line]]. * {{ill|i-Bus|de|i-Bus|ja|i-バス|zh|i公交|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/i-Bus|qq=|1=I-Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11223722}} circular bus to the Sakami Jinja-mae stop. * Immediately at the Sakami Jinja-mae intersection on {{ill|Aichi Prefectural Route 190|de|Aichi-Präfekturstraße 190|ja|愛知県道190号名古屋一宮線|zh|爱知县道190号名古宮线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefectural Route 190|qq=|1=Aichi Prefectural Road Route 190|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11494441}}. {{shinto-stub}} ==List of Motoise Shrines== {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; white-space:nowrap; font-size:85%" |- ! {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor) · {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | founded = 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | festival = April 16 | prefecture= {{ill|Imaise-chō Hon-kambe|WD=Q127432721}} }} '''Sakami Jinja''' (酒見神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]], [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and its former rank was {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. It stands on the site of the Nakashima-no-Miya where [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] once stayed, and is regarded as one of the original {{ill|Moto Ise Shrines|de|Moto-Ise-Schreine|ja|元伊勢|zh|元伊势|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto Ise Shrines|qq=|1=Moto Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11387775}}. In addition to [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the shrine also enshrines {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the ancestor of sake brewers, and {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, dedicated to [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]]. == History == When Princess Yamatohime, seeking a site to enshrine the spirit of Amaterasu Ōmikami, traveled to this area in the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] from the Ikuragawa-no-Miya in Mino Province (now [[:en:Mizuho, Gifu|Mizuho]]), she stayed at what was then known as Kōbe in Owari and enshrined the sacred object on Mount Miya. The shrine was later built by the local people. According to tradition, the original building had round pillars, a thatched roof, and an open interior. In the 3rd year of the [[:en:Saikō|Shōhei era]] (856), by imperial order of [[:en:Emperor Montoku|Emperor Montoku]], two sake brewers—Ōmura no Haji and Komura no Haji—were dispatched from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] to produce the sacred sake offerings. This event marks the site as the birthplace of sake brewing, from which the shrine’s name “Sakami” is derived. == Grounds == The shrine buildings face north, so worshippers pray facing south toward the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]]. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, featuring an open-walled design. A large jar (dated to the Kamakura period) said to have stored {{ill|kurozake|de|Schwarzsake|ja|黒酒|zh|黑酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kurozake|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神酒|1=miki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3313722}} and {{ill|shirozake|de|Weißsake|ja|白酒|zh|白酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shirozake|qq=|1=shiroki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580387}} stands beside the hall, and in front lies a stone trough once used in sake production. == Local Legends == Two unusual local legends surround this shrine. First, because the shrine faces north, it was nicknamed “Reverse Sakami Jinja” (逆見神社) after World War II. Second, the address Imaisechō Motokōbe suggests rivalry with Ise, leading to the tale that the shrine was established in competition with the Ise Grand Shrine. == Access == * 20-minute walk (about 1.5 km) from [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|Owari Ichinomiya Station]] on the [[:en:Tōkaidō Main Line|Tōkaidō Main Line]] and [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Ichinomiya Station]] on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|de|Meitetsu-Nagoya-Hauptlinie|ja|名古屋鉄道 名鉄名古屋本線|zh|名古屋铁道 名鉄名古屋本线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the [[:en:Meitetsu Bisai Line|Bisai Line]]. * {{ill|i-Bus|de|i-Bus|ja|i-バス|zh|i公交|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/i-Bus|qq=|1=I-Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11223722}} circular bus to the Sakami Jinja-mae stop. * Immediately at the Sakami Jinja-mae intersection on {{ill|Aichi Prefectural Route 190|de|Aichi-Präfekturstraße 190|ja|愛知県道190号名古屋一宮線|zh|爱知县道190号名古宮线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefectural Route 190|qq=|1=Aichi Prefectural Road Route 190|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11494441}}. {{shinto-stub}} ==List of Motoise Shrines== {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; white-space:nowrap; font-size:85%" |- ! {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
{{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor) · {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | founded = 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | festival = April 16 | prefecture= {{ill|Imaise-chō Hon-kambe|WD=Q127432721}} }} '''Sakami Jinja''' (酒見神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]], [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and its former rank was {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. It stands on the site of the Nakashima-no-Miya where [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] once stayed, and is regarded as one of the original {{ill|Moto Ise Shrines|de|Moto-Ise-Schreine|ja|元伊勢|zh|元伊势|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto Ise Shrines|qq=|1=Moto Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11387775}}. In addition to [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the shrine also enshrines {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the ancestor of sake brewers, and {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, dedicated to [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]]. == History == When Princess Yamatohime, seeking a site to enshrine the spirit of Amaterasu Ōmikami, traveled to this area in the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] from the Ikuragawa-no-Miya in Mino Province (now [[:en:Mizuho, Gifu|Mizuho]]), she stayed at what was then known as Kōbe in Owari and enshrined the sacred object on Mount Miya. The shrine was later built by the local people. According to tradition, the original building had round pillars, a thatched roof, and an open interior. In the 3rd year of the [[:en:Saikō|Shōhei era]] (856), by imperial order of [[:en:Emperor Montoku|Emperor Montoku]], two sake brewers—Ōmura no Haji and Komura no Haji—were dispatched from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] to produce the sacred sake offerings. This event marks the site as the birthplace of sake brewing, from which the shrine’s name “Sakami” is derived. == Grounds == The shrine buildings face north, so worshippers pray facing south toward the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]]. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, featuring an open-walled design. A large jar (dated to the Kamakura period) said to have stored {{ill|kurozake|de|Schwarzsake|ja|黒酒|zh|黑酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kurozake|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神酒|1=miki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3313722}} and {{ill|shirozake|de|Weißsake|ja|白酒|zh|白酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shirozake|qq=|1=shiroki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580387}} stands beside the hall, and in front lies a stone trough once used in sake production. == Local Legends == Two unusual local legends surround this shrine. First, because the shrine faces north, it was nicknamed “Reverse Sakami Jinja” (逆見神社) after World War II. Second, the address Imaisechō Motokōbe suggests rivalry with Ise, leading to the tale that the shrine was established in competition with the Ise Grand Shrine. == Access == * 20-minute walk (about 1.5 km) from [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|Owari Ichinomiya Station]] on the [[:en:Tōkaidō Main Line|Tōkaidō Main Line]] and [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Ichinomiya Station]] on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|de|Meitetsu-Nagoya-Hauptlinie|ja|名古屋鉄道 名鉄名古屋本線|zh|名古屋铁道 名鉄名古屋本线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the [[:en:Meitetsu Bisai Line|Bisai Line]]. * {{ill|i-Bus|de|i-Bus|ja|i-バス|zh|i公交|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/i-Bus|qq=|1=I-Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11223722}} circular bus to the Sakami Jinja-mae stop. * Immediately at the Sakami Jinja-mae intersection on {{ill|Aichi Prefectural Route 190|de|Aichi-Präfekturstraße 190|ja|愛知県道190号名古屋一宮線|zh|爱知县道190号名古宮线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefectural Route 190|qq=|1=Aichi Prefectural Road Route 190|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11494441}}. {{shinto-stub}} ==List of Motoise Shrines== {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; white-space:nowrap; font-size:85%" |- ! {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor) · {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | founded = 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | festival = April 16 | prefecture= {{ill|Imaise-chō Hon-kambe|WD=Q127432721}} }} '''Sakami Jinja''' (酒見神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]], [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and its former rank was {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. It stands on the site of the Nakashima-no-Miya where [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] once stayed, and is regarded as one of the original {{ill|Moto Ise Shrines|de|Moto-Ise-Schreine|ja|元伊勢|zh|元伊势|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto Ise Shrines|1=Moto Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11387775}}. In addition to [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the shrine also enshrines {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the ancestor of sake brewers, and {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, dedicated to [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]]. == History == When Princess Yamatohime, seeking a site to enshrine the spirit of Amaterasu Ōmikami, traveled to this area in the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] from the Ikuragawa-no-Miya in Mino Province (now [[:en:Mizuho, Gifu|Mizuho]]), she stayed at what was then known as Kōbe in Owari and enshrined the sacred object on Mount Miya. The shrine was later built by the local people. According to tradition, the original building had round pillars, a thatched roof, and an open interior. In the 3rd year of the [[:en:Saikō|Shōhei era]] (856), by imperial order of [[:en:Emperor Montoku|Emperor Montoku]], two sake brewers—Ōmura no Haji and Komura no Haji—were dispatched from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] to produce the sacred sake offerings. This event marks the site as the birthplace of sake brewing, from which the shrine’s name “Sakami” is derived. == Grounds == The shrine buildings face north, so worshippers pray facing south toward the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]]. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, featuring an open-walled design. A large jar (dated to the Kamakura period) said to have stored {{ill|kurozake|de|Schwarzsake|ja|黒酒|zh|黑酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kurozake|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神酒|1=miki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3313722}} and {{ill|shirozake|de|Weißsake|ja|白酒|zh|白酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shirozake|1=shiroki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580387}} stands beside the hall, and in front lies a stone trough once used in sake production. == Local Legends == Two unusual local legends surround this shrine. First, because the shrine faces north, it was nicknamed “Reverse Sakami Jinja” (逆見神社) after World War II. Second, the address Imaisechō Motokōbe suggests rivalry with Ise, leading to the tale that the shrine was established in competition with the Ise Grand Shrine. == Access == * 20-minute walk (about 1.5 km) from [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|Owari Ichinomiya Station]] on the [[:en:Tōkaidō Main Line|Tōkaidō Main Line]] and [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Ichinomiya Station]] on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|de|Meitetsu-Nagoya-Hauptlinie|ja|名古屋鉄道 名鉄名古屋本線|zh|名古屋铁道 名鉄名古屋本线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the [[:en:Meitetsu Bisai Line|Bisai Line]]. * {{ill|i-Bus|de|i-Bus|ja|i-バス|zh|i公交|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/i-Bus|1=I-Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11223722}} circular bus to the Sakami Jinja-mae stop. * Immediately at the Sakami Jinja-mae intersection on {{ill|Aichi Prefectural Route 190|de|Aichi-Präfekturstraße 190|ja|愛知県道190号名古屋一宮線|zh|爱知县道190号名古宮线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefectural Route 190|1=Aichi Prefectural Road Route 190|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11494441}}. {{shinto-stub}} ==List of Motoise Shrines== {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; white-space:nowrap; font-size:85%" |- ! {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
{{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor) · {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | founded = 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | festival = April 16 | prefecture= {{ill|Imaise-chō Hon-kambe|WD=Q127432721}} }} '''Sakami Jinja''' (酒見神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]], [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and its former rank was {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. It stands on the site of the Nakashima-no-Miya where [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] once stayed, and is regarded as one of the original {{ill|Moto Ise Shrines|de|Moto-Ise-Schreine|ja|元伊勢|zh|元伊势|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto Ise Shrines|1=Moto Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11387775}}. In addition to [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the shrine also enshrines {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the ancestor of sake brewers, and {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, dedicated to [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]]. == History == When Princess Yamatohime, seeking a site to enshrine the spirit of Amaterasu Ōmikami, traveled to this area in the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] from the Ikuragawa-no-Miya in Mino Province (now [[:en:Mizuho, Gifu|Mizuho]]), she stayed at what was then known as Kōbe in Owari and enshrined the sacred object on Mount Miya. The shrine was later built by the local people. According to tradition, the original building had round pillars, a thatched roof, and an open interior. In the 3rd year of the [[:en:Saikō|Shōhei era]] (856), by imperial order of [[:en:Emperor Montoku|Emperor Montoku]], two sake brewers—Ōmura no Haji and Komura no Haji—were dispatched from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] to produce the sacred sake offerings. This event marks the site as the birthplace of sake brewing, from which the shrine’s name “Sakami” is derived. == Grounds == The shrine buildings face north, so worshippers pray facing south toward the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]]. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, featuring an open-walled design. A large jar (dated to the Kamakura period) said to have stored {{ill|kurozake|de|Schwarzsake|ja|黒酒|zh|黑酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kurozake|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神酒|1=miki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3313722}} and {{ill|shirozake|de|Weißsake|ja|白酒|zh|白酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shirozake|1=shiroki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580387}} stands beside the hall, and in front lies a stone trough once used in sake production. == Local Legends == Two unusual local legends surround this shrine. First, because the shrine faces north, it was nicknamed “Reverse Sakami Jinja” (逆見神社) after World War II. Second, the address Imaisechō Motokōbe suggests rivalry with Ise, leading to the tale that the shrine was established in competition with the Ise Grand Shrine. == Access == * 20-minute walk (about 1.5 km) from [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|Owari Ichinomiya Station]] on the [[:en:Tōkaidō Main Line|Tōkaidō Main Line]] and [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Ichinomiya Station]] on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|de|Meitetsu-Nagoya-Hauptlinie|ja|名古屋鉄道 名鉄名古屋本線|zh|名古屋铁道 名鉄名古屋本线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the [[:en:Meitetsu Bisai Line|Bisai Line]]. * {{ill|i-Bus|de|i-Bus|ja|i-バス|zh|i公交|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/i-Bus|1=I-Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11223722}} circular bus to the Sakami Jinja-mae stop. * Immediately at the Sakami Jinja-mae intersection on {{ill|Aichi Prefectural Route 190|de|Aichi-Präfekturstraße 190|ja|愛知県道190号名古屋一宮線|zh|爱知县道190号名古宮线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefectural Route 190|1=Aichi Prefectural Road Route 190|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11494441}}. {{shinto-stub}} ==List of Motoise Shrines== {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; white-space:nowrap; font-size:85%" |- ! {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
{{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor) · {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | founded = 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | festival = April 16 | prefecture= {{ill|Imaise-chō Hon-kambe|WD=Q127432721}} }} '''Sakami Jinja''' (酒見神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]], [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and its former rank was {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. It stands on the site of the Nakashima-no-Miya where [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] once stayed, and is regarded as one of the original {{ill|Moto Ise Shrines|de|Moto-Ise-Schreine|ja|元伊勢|zh|元伊势|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto Ise Shrines|1=Moto Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11387775}}. In addition to [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the shrine also enshrines {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the ancestor of sake brewers, and {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, dedicated to [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]]. == History == When Princess Yamatohime, seeking a site to enshrine the spirit of Amaterasu Ōmikami, traveled to this area in the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] from the Ikuragawa-no-Miya in Mino Province (now [[:en:Mizuho, Gifu|Mizuho]]), she stayed at what was then known as Kōbe in Owari and enshrined the sacred object on Mount Miya. The shrine was later built by the local people. According to tradition, the original building had round pillars, a thatched roof, and an open interior. In the 3rd year of the [[:en:Saikō|Shōhei era]] (856), by imperial order of [[:en:Emperor Montoku|Emperor Montoku]], two sake brewers—Ōmura no Haji and Komura no Haji—were dispatched from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] to produce the sacred sake offerings. This event marks the site as the birthplace of sake brewing, from which the shrine’s name “Sakami” is derived. == Grounds == The shrine buildings face north, so worshippers pray facing south toward the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]]. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, featuring an open-walled design. A large jar (dated to the Kamakura period) said to have stored {{ill|kurozake|de|Schwarzsake|ja|黒酒|zh|黑酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kurozake|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神酒|1=miki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3313722}} and {{ill|shirozake|de|Weißsake|ja|白酒|zh|白酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shirozake|1=shiroki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580387}} stands beside the hall, and in front lies a stone trough once used in sake production. == Local Legends == Two unusual local legends surround this shrine. First, because the shrine faces north, it was nicknamed “Reverse Sakami Jinja” (逆見神社) after World War II. Second, the address Imaisechō Motokōbe suggests rivalry with Ise, leading to the tale that the shrine was established in competition with the Ise Grand Shrine. == Access == * 20-minute walk (about 1.5 km) from [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|Owari Ichinomiya Station]] on the [[:en:Tōkaidō Main Line|Tōkaidō Main Line]] and [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Ichinomiya Station]] on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|de|Meitetsu-Nagoya-Hauptlinie|ja|名古屋鉄道 名鉄名古屋本線|zh|名古屋铁道 名鉄名古屋本线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the [[:en:Meitetsu Bisai Line|Bisai Line]]. * {{ill|i-Bus|de|i-Bus|ja|i-バス|zh|i公交|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/i-Bus|1=I-Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11223722}} circular bus to the Sakami Jinja-mae stop. * Immediately at the Sakami Jinja-mae intersection on {{ill|Aichi Prefectural Route 190|de|Aichi-Präfekturstraße 190|ja|愛知県道190号名古屋一宮線|zh|爱知县道190号名古宮线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefectural Route 190|1=Aichi Prefectural Road Route 190|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11494441}}. {{shinto-stub}} ==List of Motoise Shrines== {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; white-space:nowrap; font-size:85%" |- ! A. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BY23AwAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA555 |title=Studies In Shinto & Shrines |date=2014-06-03 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-136-89294-3 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Army |first=United States Department of the |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PvgsAAAAIAAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=RA3-PA147 |title=Pamphlet - Dept. of the Army |date=1945 |publisher=Headquarters, Department of the Army. |language=en}}{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=MVHoAAAAMAAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA147 |title=Department of the Army Pamphlet |date=1945 |publisher=The Department |language=en}} ==Overview== {{Citation needed|date=October 27, 2014}} {{Infobox religious building | name = '''Sakami Jinja''' (酒見神社) | image = File:Sakami-jinja Shrine in Ichinomiya B.jpg | location = 1476 Miyayama, Moto-Kōbe aza, Imaisechō, [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]], [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35.315556|N|136.795|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]]
{{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
{{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor) · {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | founded = 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | festival = April 16 | prefecture= {{ill|Imaise-chō Hon-kambe|WD=Q127432721}} }} '''Sakami Jinja''' (酒見神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]], [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and its former rank was {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. It stands on the site of the Nakashima-no-Miya where [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] once stayed, and is regarded as one of the original {{ill|Moto Ise Shrines|de|Moto-Ise-Schreine|ja|元伊勢|zh|元伊势|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto Ise Shrines|1=Moto Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11387775}}. In addition to [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the shrine also enshrines {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the ancestor of sake brewers, and {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, dedicated to [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]]. == History == When Princess Yamatohime, seeking a site to enshrine the spirit of Amaterasu Ōmikami, traveled to this area in the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] from the Ikuragawa-no-Miya in Mino Province (now [[:en:Mizuho, Gifu|Mizuho]]), she stayed at what was then known as Kōbe in Owari and enshrined the sacred object on Mount Miya. The shrine was later built by the local people. According to tradition, the original building had round pillars, a thatched roof, and an open interior. In the 3rd year of the [[:en:Saikō|Shōhei era]] (856), by imperial order of [[:en:Emperor Montoku|Emperor Montoku]], two sake brewers—Ōmura no Haji and Komura no Haji—were dispatched from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] to produce the sacred sake offerings. This event marks the site as the birthplace of sake brewing, from which the shrine’s name “Sakami” is derived. == Grounds == The shrine buildings face north, so worshippers pray facing south toward the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]]. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, featuring an open-walled design. A large jar (dated to the Kamakura period) said to have stored {{ill|kurozake|de|Schwarzsake|ja|黒酒|zh|黑酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kurozake|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神酒|1=miki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3313722}} and {{ill|shirozake|de|Weißsake|ja|白酒|zh|白酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shirozake|1=shiroki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580387}} stands beside the hall, and in front lies a stone trough once used in sake production. == Local Legends == Two unusual local legends surround this shrine. First, because the shrine faces north, it was nicknamed “Reverse Sakami Jinja” (逆見神社) after World War II. Second, the address Imaisechō Motokōbe suggests rivalry with Ise, leading to the tale that the shrine was established in competition with the Ise Grand Shrine. == Access == * 20-minute walk (about 1.5 km) from [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|Owari Ichinomiya Station]] on the [[:en:Tōkaidō Main Line|Tōkaidō Main Line]] and [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Ichinomiya Station]] on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|de|Meitetsu-Nagoya-Hauptlinie|ja|名古屋鉄道 名鉄名古屋本線|zh|名古屋铁道 名鉄名古屋本线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the [[:en:Meitetsu Bisai Line|Bisai Line]]. * {{ill|i-Bus|de|i-Bus|ja|i-バス|zh|i公交|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/i-Bus|1=I-Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11223722}} circular bus to the Sakami Jinja-mae stop. * Immediately at the Sakami Jinja-mae intersection on {{ill|Aichi Prefectural Route 190|de|Aichi-Präfekturstraße 190|ja|愛知県道190号名古屋一宮線|zh|爱知县道190号名古宮线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefectural Route 190|1=Aichi Prefectural Road Route 190|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11494441}}. {{shinto-stub}} ==List of Motoise Shrines== {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; white-space:nowrap; font-size:85%" |- ! {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
{{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor) · {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | founded = 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | festival = April 16 | prefecture= {{ill|Imaise-chō Hon-kambe|WD=Q127432721}} }} '''Sakami Jinja''' (酒見神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]], [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and its former rank was {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. It stands on the site of the Nakashima-no-Miya where [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] once stayed, and is regarded as one of the original {{ill|Moto Ise Shrines|de|Moto-Ise-Schreine|ja|元伊勢|zh|元伊势|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto Ise Shrines|1=Moto Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11387775}}. In addition to [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the shrine also enshrines {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the ancestor of sake brewers, and {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, dedicated to [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]]. == History == When Princess Yamatohime, seeking a site to enshrine the spirit of Amaterasu Ōmikami, traveled to this area in the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] from the Ikuragawa-no-Miya in Mino Province (now [[:en:Mizuho, Gifu|Mizuho]]), she stayed at what was then known as Kōbe in Owari and enshrined the sacred object on Mount Miya. The shrine was later built by the local people. According to tradition, the original building had round pillars, a thatched roof, and an open interior. In the 3rd year of the [[:en:Saikō|Shōhei era]] (856), by imperial order of [[:en:Emperor Montoku|Emperor Montoku]], two sake brewers—Ōmura no Haji and Komura no Haji—were dispatched from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] to produce the sacred sake offerings. This event marks the site as the birthplace of sake brewing, from which the shrine’s name “Sakami” is derived. == Grounds == The shrine buildings face north, so worshippers pray facing south toward the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]]. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, featuring an open-walled design. A large jar (dated to the Kamakura period) said to have stored {{ill|kurozake|de|Schwarzsake|ja|黒酒|zh|黑酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kurozake|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神酒|1=miki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3313722}} and {{ill|shirozake|de|Weißsake|ja|白酒|zh|白酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shirozake|1=shiroki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580387}} stands beside the hall, and in front lies a stone trough once used in sake production. == Local Legends == Two unusual local legends surround this shrine. First, because the shrine faces north, it was nicknamed “Reverse Sakami Jinja” (逆見神社) after World War II. Second, the address Imaisechō Motokōbe suggests rivalry with Ise, leading to the tale that the shrine was established in competition with the Ise Grand Shrine. == Access == * 20-minute walk (about 1.5 km) from [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|Owari Ichinomiya Station]] on the [[:en:Tōkaidō Main Line|Tōkaidō Main Line]] and [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Ichinomiya Station]] on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|de|Meitetsu-Nagoya-Hauptlinie|ja|名古屋鉄道 名鉄名古屋本線|zh|名古屋铁道 名鉄名古屋本线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the [[:en:Meitetsu Bisai Line|Bisai Line]]. * {{ill|i-Bus|de|i-Bus|ja|i-バス|zh|i公交|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/i-Bus|1=I-Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11223722}} circular bus to the Sakami Jinja-mae stop. * Immediately at the Sakami Jinja-mae intersection on {{ill|Aichi Prefectural Route 190|de|Aichi-Präfekturstraße 190|ja|愛知県道190号名古屋一宮線|zh|爱知县道190号名古宮线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefectural Route 190|1=Aichi Prefectural Road Route 190|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11494441}}. {{shinto-stub}} ==List of Motoise Shrines== {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; white-space:nowrap; font-size:85%" |- ! {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor) · {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | founded = 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | festival = April 16 | prefecture= {{ill|Imaise-chō Hon-kambe|WD=Q127432721}} }} '''Sakami Jinja''' (酒見神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]], [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and its former rank was {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. It stands on the site of the Nakashima-no-Miya where [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] once stayed, and is regarded as one of the original {{ill|Moto Ise Shrines|de|Moto-Ise-Schreine|ja|元伊勢|zh|元伊势|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto Ise Shrines|1=Moto Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11387775}}. In addition to [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the shrine also enshrines {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the ancestor of sake brewers, and {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, dedicated to [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]]. == History == When Princess Yamatohime, seeking a site to enshrine the spirit of Amaterasu Ōmikami, traveled to this area in the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] from the Ikuragawa-no-Miya in Mino Province (now [[:en:Mizuho, Gifu|Mizuho]]), she stayed at what was then known as Kōbe in Owari and enshrined the sacred object on Mount Miya. The shrine was later built by the local people. According to tradition, the original building had round pillars, a thatched roof, and an open interior. In the 3rd year of the [[:en:Saikō|Shōhei era]] (856), by imperial order of [[:en:Emperor Montoku|Emperor Montoku]], two sake brewers—Ōmura no Haji and Komura no Haji—were dispatched from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] to produce the sacred sake offerings. This event marks the site as the birthplace of sake brewing, from which the shrine’s name “Sakami” is derived. == Grounds == The shrine buildings face north, so worshippers pray facing south toward the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]]. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, featuring an open-walled design. A large jar (dated to the Kamakura period) said to have stored {{ill|kurozake|de|Schwarzsake|ja|黒酒|zh|黑酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kurozake|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神酒|1=miki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3313722}} and {{ill|shirozake|de|Weißsake|ja|白酒|zh|白酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shirozake|1=shiroki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580387}} stands beside the hall, and in front lies a stone trough once used in sake production. == Local Legends == Two unusual local legends surround this shrine. First, because the shrine faces north, it was nicknamed “Reverse Sakami Jinja” (逆見神社) after World War II. Second, the address Imaisechō Motokōbe suggests rivalry with Ise, leading to the tale that the shrine was established in competition with the Ise Grand Shrine. == Access == * 20-minute walk (about 1.5 km) from [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|Owari Ichinomiya Station]] on the [[:en:Tōkaidō Main Line|Tōkaidō Main Line]] and [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Ichinomiya Station]] on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|de|Meitetsu-Nagoya-Hauptlinie|ja|名古屋鉄道 名鉄名古屋本線|zh|名古屋铁道 名鉄名古屋本线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the [[:en:Meitetsu Bisai Line|Bisai Line]]. * {{ill|i-Bus|de|i-Bus|ja|i-バス|zh|i公交|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/i-Bus|1=I-Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11223722}} circular bus to the Sakami Jinja-mae stop. * Immediately at the Sakami Jinja-mae intersection on {{ill|Aichi Prefectural Route 190|de|Aichi-Präfekturstraße 190|ja|愛知県道190号名古屋一宮線|zh|爱知县道190号名古宮线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefectural Route 190|1=Aichi Prefectural Road Route 190|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11494441}}. {{shinto-stub}} ==List of Motoise Shrines== {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; white-space:nowrap; font-size:85%" |- ! {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
{{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor) · {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | founded = 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | festival = April 16 | prefecture= {{ill|Imaise-chō Hon-kambe|WD=Q127432721}} }} '''Sakami Jinja''' (酒見神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]], [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and its former rank was {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. It stands on the site of the Nakashima-no-Miya where [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] once stayed, and is regarded as one of the original {{ill|Moto Ise Shrines|de|Moto-Ise-Schreine|ja|元伊勢|zh|元伊势|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto Ise Shrines|1=Moto Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11387775}}. In addition to [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the shrine also enshrines {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the ancestor of sake brewers, and {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, dedicated to [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]]. == History == When Princess Yamatohime, seeking a site to enshrine the spirit of Amaterasu Ōmikami, traveled to this area in the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] from the Ikuragawa-no-Miya in Mino Province (now [[:en:Mizuho, Gifu|Mizuho]]), she stayed at what was then known as Kōbe in Owari and enshrined the sacred object on Mount Miya. The shrine was later built by the local people. According to tradition, the original building had round pillars, a thatched roof, and an open interior. In the 3rd year of the [[:en:Saikō|Shōhei era]] (856), by imperial order of [[:en:Emperor Montoku|Emperor Montoku]], two sake brewers—Ōmura no Haji and Komura no Haji—were dispatched from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] to produce the sacred sake offerings. This event marks the site as the birthplace of sake brewing, from which the shrine’s name “Sakami” is derived. == Grounds == The shrine buildings face north, so worshippers pray facing south toward the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]]. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, featuring an open-walled design. A large jar (dated to the Kamakura period) said to have stored {{ill|kurozake|de|Schwarzsake|ja|黒酒|zh|黑酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kurozake|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神酒|1=miki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3313722}} and {{ill|shirozake|de|Weißsake|ja|白酒|zh|白酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shirozake|1=shiroki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580387}} stands beside the hall, and in front lies a stone trough once used in sake production. == Local Legends == Two unusual local legends surround this shrine. First, because the shrine faces north, it was nicknamed “Reverse Sakami Jinja” (逆見神社) after World War II. Second, the address Imaisechō Motokōbe suggests rivalry with Ise, leading to the tale that the shrine was established in competition with the Ise Grand Shrine. == Access == * 20-minute walk (about 1.5 km) from [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|Owari Ichinomiya Station]] on the [[:en:Tōkaidō Main Line|Tōkaidō Main Line]] and [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Ichinomiya Station]] on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|de|Meitetsu-Nagoya-Hauptlinie|ja|名古屋鉄道 名鉄名古屋本線|zh|名古屋铁道 名鉄名古屋本线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the [[:en:Meitetsu Bisai Line|Bisai Line]]. * {{ill|i-Bus|de|i-Bus|ja|i-バス|zh|i公交|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/i-Bus|1=I-Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11223722}} circular bus to the Sakami Jinja-mae stop. * Immediately at the Sakami Jinja-mae intersection on {{ill|Aichi Prefectural Route 190|de|Aichi-Präfekturstraße 190|ja|愛知県道190号名古屋一宮線|zh|爱知县道190号名古宮线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefectural Route 190|1=Aichi Prefectural Road Route 190|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11494441}}. {{shinto-stub}} ==List of Motoise Shrines== {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; white-space:nowrap; font-size:85%" |- ! {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
{{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor) · {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | founded = 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | festival = April 16 | prefecture= {{ill|Imaise-chō Hon-kambe|WD=Q127432721}} }} '''Sakami Jinja''' (酒見神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]], [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and its former rank was {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. It stands on the site of the Nakashima-no-Miya where [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] once stayed, and is regarded as one of the original {{ill|Moto Ise Shrines|de|Moto-Ise-Schreine|ja|元伊勢|zh|元伊势|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto Ise Shrines|1=Moto Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11387775}}. In addition to [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the shrine also enshrines {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the ancestor of sake brewers, and {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, dedicated to [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]]. == History == When Princess Yamatohime, seeking a site to enshrine the spirit of Amaterasu Ōmikami, traveled to this area in the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] from the Ikuragawa-no-Miya in Mino Province (now [[:en:Mizuho, Gifu|Mizuho]]), she stayed at what was then known as Kōbe in Owari and enshrined the sacred object on Mount Miya. The shrine was later built by the local people. According to tradition, the original building had round pillars, a thatched roof, and an open interior. In the 3rd year of the [[:en:Saikō|Shōhei era]] (856), by imperial order of [[:en:Emperor Montoku|Emperor Montoku]], two sake brewers—Ōmura no Haji and Komura no Haji—were dispatched from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] to produce the sacred sake offerings. This event marks the site as the birthplace of sake brewing, from which the shrine’s name “Sakami” is derived. == Grounds == The shrine buildings face north, so worshippers pray facing south toward the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]]. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, featuring an open-walled design. A large jar (dated to the Kamakura period) said to have stored {{ill|kurozake|de|Schwarzsake|ja|黒酒|zh|黑酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kurozake|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神酒|1=miki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3313722}} and {{ill|shirozake|de|Weißsake|ja|白酒|zh|白酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shirozake|1=shiroki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580387}} stands beside the hall, and in front lies a stone trough once used in sake production. == Local Legends == Two unusual local legends surround this shrine. First, because the shrine faces north, it was nicknamed “Reverse Sakami Jinja” (逆見神社) after World War II. Second, the address Imaisechō Motokōbe suggests rivalry with Ise, leading to the tale that the shrine was established in competition with the Ise Grand Shrine. == Access == * 20-minute walk (about 1.5 km) from [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|Owari Ichinomiya Station]] on the [[:en:Tōkaidō Main Line|Tōkaidō Main Line]] and [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Ichinomiya Station]] on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|de|Meitetsu-Nagoya-Hauptlinie|ja|名古屋鉄道 名鉄名古屋本線|zh|名古屋铁道 名鉄名古屋本线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the [[:en:Meitetsu Bisai Line|Bisai Line]]. * {{ill|i-Bus|de|i-Bus|ja|i-バス|zh|i公交|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/i-Bus|1=I-Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11223722}} circular bus to the Sakami Jinja-mae stop. * Immediately at the Sakami Jinja-mae intersection on {{ill|Aichi Prefectural Route 190|de|Aichi-Präfekturstraße 190|ja|愛知県道190号名古屋一宮線|zh|爱知县道190号名古宮线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefectural Route 190|1=Aichi Prefectural Road Route 190|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11494441}}. {{shinto-stub}} ==List of Motoise Shrines== {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; white-space:nowrap; font-size:85%" |- !
