{{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
{{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor) · {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | founded = 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | festival = April 16 | prefecture= {{ill|Imaise-chō Hon-kambe|WD=Q127432721}} }} '''Sakami Jinja''' (酒見神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]], [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and its former rank was {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. It stands on the site of the Nakashima-no-Miya where [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] once stayed, and is regarded as one of the original {{ill|Moto Ise Shrines|de|Moto-Ise-Schreine|ja|元伊勢|zh|元伊势|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto Ise Shrines|1=Moto Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11387775}}. In addition to [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the shrine also enshrines {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the ancestor of sake brewers, and {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, dedicated to [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]]. == History == When Princess Yamatohime, seeking a site to enshrine the spirit of Amaterasu Ōmikami, traveled to this area in the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] from the Ikuragawa-no-Miya in Mino Province (now [[:en:Mizuho, Gifu|Mizuho]]), she stayed at what was then known as Kōbe in Owari and enshrined the sacred object on Mount Miya. The shrine was later built by the local people. According to tradition, the original building had round pillars, a thatched roof, and an open interior. In the 3rd year of the [[:en:Saikō|Shōhei era]] (856), by imperial order of [[:en:Emperor Montoku|Emperor Montoku]], two sake brewers—Ōmura no Haji and Komura no Haji—were dispatched from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] to produce the sacred sake offerings. This event marks the site as the birthplace of sake brewing, from which the shrine’s name “Sakami” is derived. == Grounds == The shrine buildings face north, so worshippers pray facing south toward the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]]. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, featuring an open-walled design. A large jar (dated to the Kamakura period) said to have stored {{ill|kurozake|de|Schwarzsake|ja|黒酒|zh|黑酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kurozake|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神酒|1=miki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3313722}} and {{ill|shirozake|de|Weißsake|ja|白酒|zh|白酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shirozake|1=shiroki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580387}} stands beside the hall, and in front lies a stone trough once used in sake production. == Local Legends == Two unusual local legends surround this shrine. First, because the shrine faces north, it was nicknamed “Reverse Sakami Jinja” (逆見神社) after World War II. Second, the address Imaisechō Motokōbe suggests rivalry with Ise, leading to the tale that the shrine was established in competition with the Ise Grand Shrine. == Access == * 20-minute walk (about 1.5 km) from [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|Owari Ichinomiya Station]] on the [[:en:Tōkaidō Main Line|Tōkaidō Main Line]] and [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Ichinomiya Station]] on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|de|Meitetsu-Nagoya-Hauptlinie|ja|名古屋鉄道 名鉄名古屋本線|zh|名古屋铁道 名鉄名古屋本线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the [[:en:Meitetsu Bisai Line|Bisai Line]]. * {{ill|i-Bus|de|i-Bus|ja|i-バス|zh|i公交|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/i-Bus|1=I-Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11223722}} circular bus to the Sakami Jinja-mae stop. * Immediately at the Sakami Jinja-mae intersection on {{ill|Aichi Prefectural Route 190|de|Aichi-Präfekturstraße 190|ja|愛知県道190号名古屋一宮線|zh|爱知县道190号名古宮线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefectural Route 190|1=Aichi Prefectural Road Route 190|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11494441}}. {{shinto-stub}} ==List of Motoise Shrines== {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; white-space:nowrap; font-size:85%" |- ! {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor) · {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | founded = 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | festival = April 16 | prefecture= {{ill|Imaise-chō Hon-kambe|WD=Q127432721}} }} '''Sakami Jinja''' (酒見神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]], [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and its former rank was {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. It stands on the site of the Nakashima-no-Miya where [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] once stayed, and is regarded as one of the original {{ill|Moto Ise Shrines|de|Moto-Ise-Schreine|ja|元伊勢|zh|元伊势|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto Ise Shrines|1=Moto Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11387775}}. In addition to [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the shrine also enshrines {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the ancestor of sake brewers, and {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, dedicated to [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]]. == History == When Princess Yamatohime, seeking a site to enshrine the spirit of Amaterasu Ōmikami, traveled to this area in the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] from the Ikuragawa-no-Miya in Mino Province (now [[:en:Mizuho, Gifu|Mizuho]]), she stayed at what was then known as Kōbe in Owari and enshrined the sacred object on Mount Miya. The shrine was later built by the local people. According to tradition, the original building had round pillars, a thatched roof, and an open interior. In the 3rd year of the [[:en:Saikō|Shōhei era]] (856), by imperial order of [[:en:Emperor Montoku|Emperor Montoku]], two sake brewers—Ōmura no Haji and Komura no Haji—were dispatched from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] to produce the sacred sake offerings. This event marks the site as the birthplace of sake brewing, from which the shrine’s name “Sakami” is derived. == Grounds == The shrine buildings face north, so worshippers pray facing south toward the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]]. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, featuring an open-walled design. A large jar (dated to the Kamakura period) said to have stored {{ill|kurozake|de|Schwarzsake|ja|黒酒|zh|黑酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kurozake|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神酒|1=miki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3313722}} and {{ill|shirozake|de|Weißsake|ja|白酒|zh|白酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shirozake|1=shiroki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580387}} stands beside the hall, and in front lies a stone trough once used in sake production. == Local Legends == Two unusual local legends surround this shrine. First, because the shrine faces north, it was nicknamed “Reverse Sakami Jinja” (逆見神社) after World War II. Second, the address Imaisechō Motokōbe suggests rivalry with Ise, leading to the tale that the shrine was established in competition with the Ise Grand Shrine. == Access == * 20-minute walk (about 1.5 km) from [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|Owari Ichinomiya Station]] on the [[:en:Tōkaidō Main Line|Tōkaidō Main Line]] and [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Ichinomiya Station]] on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|de|Meitetsu-Nagoya-Hauptlinie|ja|名古屋鉄道 名鉄名古屋本線|zh|名古屋铁道 名鉄名古屋本线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the [[:en:Meitetsu Bisai Line|Bisai Line]]. * {{ill|i-Bus|de|i-Bus|ja|i-バス|zh|i公交|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/i-Bus|1=I-Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11223722}} circular bus to the Sakami Jinja-mae stop. * Immediately at the Sakami Jinja-mae intersection on {{ill|Aichi Prefectural Route 190|de|Aichi-Präfekturstraße 190|ja|愛知県道190号名古屋一宮線|zh|爱知县道190号名古宮线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefectural Route 190|1=Aichi Prefectural Road Route 190|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11494441}}. {{shinto-stub}} ==List of Motoise Shrines== {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; white-space:nowrap; font-size:85%" |- ! {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor) · {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | founded = 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | festival = April 16 | prefecture= {{ill|Imaise-chō Hon-kambe|WD=Q127432721}} }} '''Sakami Jinja''' (酒見神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]], [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and its former rank was {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. It stands on the site of the Nakashima-no-Miya where [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] once stayed, and is regarded as one of the original {{ill|Moto Ise Shrines|de|Moto-Ise-Schreine|ja|元伊勢|zh|元伊势|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto Ise Shrines|1=Moto Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11387775}}. In addition to [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the shrine also enshrines {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the ancestor of sake brewers, and {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, dedicated to [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]]. == History == When Princess Yamatohime, seeking a site to enshrine the spirit of Amaterasu Ōmikami, traveled to this area in the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] from the Ikuragawa-no-Miya in Mino Province (now [[:en:Mizuho, Gifu|Mizuho]]), she stayed at what was then known as Kōbe in Owari and enshrined the sacred object on Mount Miya. The shrine was later built by the local people. According to tradition, the original building had round pillars, a thatched roof, and an open interior. In the 3rd year of the [[:en:Saikō|Shōhei era]] (856), by imperial order of [[:en:Emperor Montoku|Emperor Montoku]], two sake brewers—Ōmura no Haji and Komura no Haji—were dispatched from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] to produce the sacred sake offerings. This event marks the site as the birthplace of sake brewing, from which the shrine’s name “Sakami” is derived. == Grounds == The shrine buildings face north, so worshippers pray facing south toward the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]]. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, featuring an open-walled design. A large jar (dated to the Kamakura period) said to have stored {{ill|kurozake|de|Schwarzsake|ja|黒酒|zh|黑酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kurozake|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神酒|1=miki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3313722}} and {{ill|shirozake|de|Weißsake|ja|白酒|zh|白酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shirozake|1=shiroki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580387}} stands beside the hall, and in front lies a stone trough once used in sake production. == Local Legends == Two unusual local legends surround this shrine. First, because the shrine faces north, it was nicknamed “Reverse Sakami Jinja” (逆見神社) after World War II. Second, the address Imaisechō Motokōbe suggests rivalry with Ise, leading to the tale that the shrine was established in competition with the Ise Grand Shrine. == Access == * 20-minute walk (about 1.5 km) from [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|Owari Ichinomiya Station]] on the [[:en:Tōkaidō Main Line|Tōkaidō Main Line]] and [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Ichinomiya Station]] on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|de|Meitetsu-Nagoya-Hauptlinie|ja|名古屋鉄道 名鉄名古屋本線|zh|名古屋铁道 名鉄名古屋本线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the [[:en:Meitetsu Bisai Line|Bisai Line]]. * {{ill|i-Bus|de|i-Bus|ja|i-バス|zh|i公交|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/i-Bus|1=I-Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11223722}} circular bus to the Sakami Jinja-mae stop. * Immediately at the Sakami Jinja-mae intersection on {{ill|Aichi Prefectural Route 190|de|Aichi-Präfekturstraße 190|ja|愛知県道190号名古屋一宮線|zh|爱知县道190号名古宮线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefectural Route 190|1=Aichi Prefectural Road Route 190|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11494441}}. {{shinto-stub}} ==List of Motoise Shrines== {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; white-space:nowrap; font-size:85%" |- ! It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and its former rank was {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. It stands on the site of the Nakashima-no-Miya where [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] once stayed, and is regarded as one of the original {{ill|Moto Ise Shrines|de|Moto-Ise-Schreine|ja|元伊勢|zh|元伊势|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto Ise Shrines|1=Moto Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11387775}}. In addition to [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the shrine also enshrines {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the ancestor of sake brewers, and {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, dedicated to [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]]. == History == When Princess Yamatohime, seeking a site to enshrine the spirit of Amaterasu Ōmikami, traveled to this area in the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] from the Ikuragawa-no-Miya in Mino Province (now [[:en:Mizuho, Gifu|Mizuho]]), she stayed at what was then known as Kōbe in Owari and enshrined the sacred object on Mount Miya. The shrine was later built by the local people. According to tradition, the original building had round pillars, a thatched roof, and an open interior. In the 3rd year of the [[:en:Saikō|Shōhei era]] (856), by imperial order of [[:en:Emperor Montoku|Emperor Montoku]], two sake brewers—Ōmura no Haji and Komura no Haji—were dispatched from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] to produce the sacred sake offerings. This event marks the site as the birthplace of sake brewing, from which the shrine’s name “Sakami” is derived. == Grounds == The shrine buildings face north, so worshippers pray facing south toward the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]]. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, featuring an open-walled design. A large jar (dated to the Kamakura period) said to have stored {{ill|kurozake|de|Schwarzsake|ja|黒酒|zh|黑酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kurozake|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神酒|1=miki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3313722}} and {{ill|shirozake|de|Weißsake|ja|白酒|zh|白酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shirozake|1=shiroki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580387}} stands beside the hall, and in front lies a stone trough once used in sake production. == Local Legends == Two unusual local legends surround this shrine. First, because the shrine faces north, it was nicknamed “Reverse Sakami Jinja” (逆見神社) after World War II. Second, the address Imaisechō Motokōbe suggests rivalry with Ise, leading to the tale that the shrine was established in competition with the Ise Grand Shrine. == Access == * 20-minute walk (about 1.5 km) from [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|Owari Ichinomiya Station]] on the [[:en:Tōkaidō Main Line|Tōkaidō Main Line]] and [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Ichinomiya Station]] on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|de|Meitetsu-Nagoya-Hauptlinie|ja|名古屋鉄道 名鉄名古屋本線|zh|名古屋铁道 名鉄名古屋本线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the [[:en:Meitetsu Bisai Line|Bisai Line]]. * {{ill|i-Bus|de|i-Bus|ja|i-バス|zh|i公交|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/i-Bus|1=I-Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11223722}} circular bus to the Sakami Jinja-mae stop. * Immediately at the Sakami Jinja-mae intersection on {{ill|Aichi Prefectural Route 190|de|Aichi-Präfekturstraße 190|ja|愛知県道190号名古屋一宮線|zh|爱知县道190号名古宮线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefectural Route 190|1=Aichi Prefectural Road Route 190|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11494441}}. {{shinto-stub}} ==List of Motoise Shrines== {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; white-space:nowrap; font-size:85%" |- ! {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor) · {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | founded = 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | festival = April 16 | prefecture= {{ill|Imaise-chō Hon-kambe|WD=Q127432721}} }} '''Sakami Jinja''' (酒見神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]], [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and its former rank was {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. It stands on the site of the Nakashima-no-Miya where [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] once stayed, and is regarded as one of the original {{ill|Moto Ise Shrines|de|Moto-Ise-Schreine|ja|元伊勢|zh|元伊势|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto Ise Shrines|1=Moto Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11387775}}. In addition to [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the shrine also enshrines {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the ancestor of sake brewers, and {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, dedicated to [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]]. == History == When Princess Yamatohime, seeking a site to enshrine the spirit of Amaterasu Ōmikami, traveled to this area in the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] from the Ikuragawa-no-Miya in Mino Province (now [[:en:Mizuho, Gifu|Mizuho]]), she stayed at what was then known as Kōbe in Owari and enshrined the sacred object on Mount Miya. The shrine was later built by the local people. According to tradition, the original building had round pillars, a thatched roof, and an open interior. In the 3rd year of the [[:en:Saikō|Shōhei era]] (856), by imperial order of [[:en:Emperor Montoku|Emperor Montoku]], two sake brewers—Ōmura no Haji and Komura no Haji—were dispatched from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] to produce the sacred sake offerings. This event marks the site as the birthplace of sake brewing, from which the shrine’s name “Sakami” is derived. == Grounds == The shrine buildings face north, so worshippers pray facing south toward the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]]. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, featuring an open-walled design. A large jar (dated to the Kamakura period) said to have stored {{ill|kurozake|de|Schwarzsake|ja|黒酒|zh|黑酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kurozake|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神酒|1=miki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3313722}} and {{ill|shirozake|de|Weißsake|ja|白酒|zh|白酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shirozake|1=shiroki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580387}} stands beside the hall, and in front lies a stone trough once used in sake production. == Local Legends == Two unusual local legends surround this shrine. First, because the shrine faces north, it was nicknamed “Reverse Sakami Jinja” (逆見神社) after World War II. Second, the address Imaisechō Motokōbe suggests rivalry with Ise, leading to the tale that the shrine was established in competition with the Ise Grand Shrine. == Access == * 20-minute walk (about 1.5 km) from [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|Owari Ichinomiya Station]] on the [[:en:Tōkaidō Main Line|Tōkaidō Main Line]] and [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Ichinomiya Station]] on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|de|Meitetsu-Nagoya-Hauptlinie|ja|名古屋鉄道 名鉄名古屋本線|zh|名古屋铁道 名鉄名古屋本线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the [[:en:Meitetsu Bisai Line|Bisai Line]]. * {{ill|i-Bus|de|i-Bus|ja|i-バス|zh|i公交|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/i-Bus|1=I-Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11223722}} circular bus to the Sakami Jinja-mae stop. * Immediately at the Sakami Jinja-mae intersection on {{ill|Aichi Prefectural Route 190|de|Aichi-Präfekturstraße 190|ja|愛知県道190号名古屋一宮線|zh|爱知县道190号名古宮线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefectural Route 190|1=Aichi Prefectural Road Route 190|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11494441}}. {{shinto-stub}} ==List of Motoise Shrines== {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; white-space:nowrap; font-size:85%" |- ! {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
{{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor) · {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | founded = 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | festival = April 16 | prefecture= {{ill|Imaise-chō Hon-kambe|WD=Q127432721}} }} '''Sakami Jinja''' (酒見神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]], [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and its former rank was {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. It stands on the site of the Nakashima-no-Miya where [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] once stayed, and is regarded as one of the original {{ill|Moto Ise Shrines|de|Moto-Ise-Schreine|ja|元伊勢|zh|元伊势|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto Ise Shrines|1=Moto Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11387775}}. In addition to [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the shrine also enshrines {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the ancestor of sake brewers, and {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, dedicated to [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]]. == History == When Princess Yamatohime, seeking a site to enshrine the spirit of Amaterasu Ōmikami, traveled to this area in the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] from the Ikuragawa-no-Miya in Mino Province (now [[:en:Mizuho, Gifu|Mizuho]]), she stayed at what was then known as Kōbe in Owari and enshrined the sacred object on Mount Miya. The shrine was later built by the local people. According to tradition, the original building had round pillars, a thatched roof, and an open interior. In the 3rd year of the [[:en:Saikō|Shōhei era]] (856), by imperial order of [[:en:Emperor Montoku|Emperor Montoku]], two sake brewers—Ōmura no Haji and Komura no Haji—were dispatched from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] to produce the sacred sake offerings. This event marks the site as the birthplace of sake brewing, from which the shrine’s name “Sakami” is derived. == Grounds == The shrine buildings face north, so worshippers pray facing south toward the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]]. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, featuring an open-walled design. A large jar (dated to the Kamakura period) said to have stored {{ill|kurozake|de|Schwarzsake|ja|黒酒|zh|黑酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kurozake|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神酒|1=miki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3313722}} and {{ill|shirozake|de|Weißsake|ja|白酒|zh|白酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shirozake|1=shiroki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580387}} stands beside the hall, and in front lies a stone trough once used in sake production. == Local Legends == Two unusual local legends surround this shrine. First, because the shrine faces north, it was nicknamed “Reverse Sakami Jinja” (逆見神社) after World War II. Second, the address Imaisechō Motokōbe suggests rivalry with Ise, leading to the tale that the shrine was established in competition with the Ise Grand Shrine. == Access == * 20-minute walk (about 1.5 km) from [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|Owari Ichinomiya Station]] on the [[:en:Tōkaidō Main Line|Tōkaidō Main Line]] and [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Ichinomiya Station]] on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|de|Meitetsu-Nagoya-Hauptlinie|ja|名古屋鉄道 名鉄名古屋本線|zh|名古屋铁道 名鉄名古屋本线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the [[:en:Meitetsu Bisai Line|Bisai Line]]. * {{ill|i-Bus|de|i-Bus|ja|i-バス|zh|i公交|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/i-Bus|1=I-Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11223722}} circular bus to the Sakami Jinja-mae stop. * Immediately at the Sakami Jinja-mae intersection on {{ill|Aichi Prefectural Route 190|de|Aichi-Präfekturstraße 190|ja|愛知県道190号名古屋一宮線|zh|爱知县道190号名古宮线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefectural Route 190|1=Aichi Prefectural Road Route 190|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11494441}}. {{shinto-stub}} ==List of Motoise Shrines== {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; white-space:nowrap; font-size:85%" |- ! {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
{{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor) · {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | founded = 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | festival = April 16 | prefecture= {{ill|Imaise-chō Hon-kambe|WD=Q127432721}} }} '''Sakami Jinja''' (酒見神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]], [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and its former rank was {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. It stands on the site of the Nakashima-no-Miya where [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] once stayed, and is regarded as one of the original {{ill|Moto Ise Shrines|de|Moto-Ise-Schreine|ja|元伊勢|zh|元伊势|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto Ise Shrines|1=Moto Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11387775}}. In addition to [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the shrine also enshrines {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the ancestor of sake brewers, and {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, dedicated to [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]]. == History == When Princess Yamatohime, seeking a site to enshrine the spirit of Amaterasu Ōmikami, traveled to this area in the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] from the Ikuragawa-no-Miya in Mino Province (now [[:en:Mizuho, Gifu|Mizuho]]), she stayed at what was then known as Kōbe in Owari and enshrined the sacred object on Mount Miya. The shrine was later built by the local people. According to tradition, the original building had round pillars, a thatched roof, and an open interior. In the 3rd year of the [[:en:Saikō|Shōhei era]] (856), by imperial order of [[:en:Emperor Montoku|Emperor Montoku]], two sake brewers—Ōmura no Haji and Komura no Haji—were dispatched from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] to produce the sacred sake offerings. This event marks the site as the birthplace of sake brewing, from which the shrine’s name “Sakami” is derived. == Grounds == The shrine buildings face north, so worshippers pray facing south toward the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]]. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, featuring an open-walled design. A large jar (dated to the Kamakura period) said to have stored {{ill|kurozake|de|Schwarzsake|ja|黒酒|zh|黑酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kurozake|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神酒|1=miki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3313722}} and {{ill|shirozake|de|Weißsake|ja|白酒|zh|白酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shirozake|1=shiroki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580387}} stands beside the hall, and in front lies a stone trough once used in sake production. == Local Legends == Two unusual local legends surround this shrine. First, because the shrine faces north, it was nicknamed “Reverse Sakami Jinja” (逆見神社) after World War II. Second, the address Imaisechō Motokōbe suggests rivalry with Ise, leading to the tale that the shrine was established in competition with the Ise Grand Shrine. == Access == * 20-minute walk (about 1.5 km) from [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|Owari Ichinomiya Station]] on the [[:en:Tōkaidō Main Line|Tōkaidō Main Line]] and [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Ichinomiya Station]] on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|de|Meitetsu-Nagoya-Hauptlinie|ja|名古屋鉄道 名鉄名古屋本線|zh|名古屋铁道 名鉄名古屋本线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the [[:en:Meitetsu Bisai Line|Bisai Line]]. * {{ill|i-Bus|de|i-Bus|ja|i-バス|zh|i公交|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/i-Bus|1=I-Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11223722}} circular bus to the Sakami Jinja-mae stop. * Immediately at the Sakami Jinja-mae intersection on {{ill|Aichi Prefectural Route 190|de|Aichi-Präfekturstraße 190|ja|愛知県道190号名古屋一宮線|zh|爱知县道190号名古宮线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefectural Route 190|1=Aichi Prefectural Road Route 190|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11494441}}. {{shinto-stub}} ==List of Motoise Shrines== {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; white-space:nowrap; font-size:85%" |- ! B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BY23AwAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA555 |title=Studies In Shinto & Shrines |date=2014-06-03 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-136-89294-3 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Army |first=United States Department of the |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PvgsAAAAIAAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=RA3-PA147 |title=Pamphlet - Dept. of the Army |date=1945 |publisher=Headquarters, Department of the Army. |language=en}}{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=MVHoAAAAMAAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA147 |title=Department of the Army Pamphlet |date=1945 |publisher=The Department |language=en}} ==Overview== {{Citation needed|date=October 27, 2014}} {{Infobox religious building | name = '''Sakami Jinja''' (酒見神社) | image = File:Sakami-jinja Shrine in Ichinomiya B.jpg | location = 1476 Miyayama, Moto-Kōbe aza, Imaisechō, [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]], [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35.315556|N|136.795|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]]
{{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
{{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor) · {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | founded = 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | festival = April 16 | prefecture= {{ill|Imaise-chō Hon-kambe|WD=Q127432721}} }} '''Sakami Jinja''' (酒見神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]], [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and its former rank was {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. It stands on the site of the Nakashima-no-Miya where [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] once stayed, and is regarded as one of the original {{ill|Moto Ise Shrines|de|Moto-Ise-Schreine|ja|元伊勢|zh|元伊势|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto Ise Shrines|1=Moto Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11387775}}. In addition to [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the shrine also enshrines {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the ancestor of sake brewers, and {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, dedicated to [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]]. == History == When Princess Yamatohime, seeking a site to enshrine the spirit of Amaterasu Ōmikami, traveled to this area in the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] from the Ikuragawa-no-Miya in Mino Province (now [[:en:Mizuho, Gifu|Mizuho]]), she stayed at what was then known as Kōbe in Owari and enshrined the sacred object on Mount Miya. The shrine was later built by the local people. According to tradition, the original building had round pillars, a thatched roof, and an open interior. In the 3rd year of the [[:en:Saikō|Shōhei era]] (856), by imperial order of [[:en:Emperor Montoku|Emperor Montoku]], two sake brewers—Ōmura no Haji and Komura no Haji—were dispatched from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] to produce the sacred sake offerings. This event marks the site as the birthplace of sake brewing, from which the shrine’s name “Sakami” is derived. == Grounds == The shrine buildings face north, so worshippers pray facing south toward the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]]. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, featuring an open-walled design. A large jar (dated to the Kamakura period) said to have stored {{ill|kurozake|de|Schwarzsake|ja|黒酒|zh|黑酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kurozake|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神酒|1=miki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3313722}} and {{ill|shirozake|de|Weißsake|ja|白酒|zh|白酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shirozake|1=shiroki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580387}} stands beside the hall, and in front lies a stone trough once used in sake production. == Local Legends == Two unusual local legends surround this shrine. First, because the shrine faces north, it was nicknamed “Reverse Sakami Jinja” (逆見神社) after World War II. Second, the address Imaisechō Motokōbe suggests rivalry with Ise, leading to the tale that the shrine was established in competition with the Ise Grand Shrine. == Access == * 20-minute walk (about 1.5 km) from [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|Owari Ichinomiya Station]] on the [[:en:Tōkaidō Main Line|Tōkaidō Main Line]] and [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Ichinomiya Station]] on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|de|Meitetsu-Nagoya-Hauptlinie|ja|名古屋鉄道 名鉄名古屋本線|zh|名古屋铁道 名鉄名古屋本线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the [[:en:Meitetsu Bisai Line|Bisai Line]]. * {{ill|i-Bus|de|i-Bus|ja|i-バス|zh|i公交|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/i-Bus|1=I-Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11223722}} circular bus to the Sakami Jinja-mae stop. * Immediately at the Sakami Jinja-mae intersection on {{ill|Aichi Prefectural Route 190|de|Aichi-Präfekturstraße 190|ja|愛知県道190号名古屋一宮線|zh|爱知县道190号名古宮线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefectural Route 190|1=Aichi Prefectural Road Route 190|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11494441}}. {{shinto-stub}} ==List of Motoise Shrines== {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; white-space:nowrap; font-size:85%" |- ! {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
{{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor) · {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | founded = 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | festival = April 16 | prefecture= {{ill|Imaise-chō Hon-kambe|WD=Q127432721}} }} '''Sakami Jinja''' (酒見神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]], [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and its former rank was {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. It stands on the site of the Nakashima-no-Miya where [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] once stayed, and is regarded as one of the original {{ill|Moto Ise Shrines|de|Moto-Ise-Schreine|ja|元伊勢|zh|元伊势|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto Ise Shrines|1=Moto Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11387775}}. In addition to [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the shrine also enshrines {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the ancestor of sake brewers, and {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, dedicated to [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]]. == History == When Princess Yamatohime, seeking a site to enshrine the spirit of Amaterasu Ōmikami, traveled to this area in the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] from the Ikuragawa-no-Miya in Mino Province (now [[:en:Mizuho, Gifu|Mizuho]]), she stayed at what was then known as Kōbe in Owari and enshrined the sacred object on Mount Miya. The shrine was later built by the local people. According to tradition, the original building had round pillars, a thatched roof, and an open interior. In the 3rd year of the [[:en:Saikō|Shōhei era]] (856), by imperial order of [[:en:Emperor Montoku|Emperor Montoku]], two sake brewers—Ōmura no Haji and Komura no Haji—were dispatched from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] to produce the sacred sake offerings. This event marks the site as the birthplace of sake brewing, from which the shrine’s name “Sakami” is derived. == Grounds == The shrine buildings face north, so worshippers pray facing south toward the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]]. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, featuring an open-walled design. A large jar (dated to the Kamakura period) said to have stored {{ill|kurozake|de|Schwarzsake|ja|黒酒|zh|黑酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kurozake|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神酒|1=miki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3313722}} and {{ill|shirozake|de|Weißsake|ja|白酒|zh|白酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shirozake|1=shiroki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580387}} stands beside the hall, and in front lies a stone trough once used in sake production. == Local Legends == Two unusual local legends surround this shrine. First, because the shrine faces north, it was nicknamed “Reverse Sakami Jinja” (逆見神社) after World War II. Second, the address Imaisechō Motokōbe suggests rivalry with Ise, leading to the tale that the shrine was established in competition with the Ise Grand Shrine. == Access == * 20-minute walk (about 1.5 km) from [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|Owari Ichinomiya Station]] on the [[:en:Tōkaidō Main Line|Tōkaidō Main Line]] and [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Ichinomiya Station]] on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|de|Meitetsu-Nagoya-Hauptlinie|ja|名古屋鉄道 名鉄名古屋本線|zh|名古屋铁道 名鉄名古屋本线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the [[:en:Meitetsu Bisai Line|Bisai Line]]. * {{ill|i-Bus|de|i-Bus|ja|i-バス|zh|i公交|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/i-Bus|1=I-Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11223722}} circular bus to the Sakami Jinja-mae stop. * Immediately at the Sakami Jinja-mae intersection on {{ill|Aichi Prefectural Route 190|de|Aichi-Präfekturstraße 190|ja|愛知県道190号名古屋一宮線|zh|爱知县道190号名古宮线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefectural Route 190|1=Aichi Prefectural Road Route 190|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11494441}}. {{shinto-stub}} ==List of Motoise Shrines== {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; white-space:nowrap; font-size:85%" |- ! {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
{{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor) · {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | founded = 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | festival = April 16 | prefecture= {{ill|Imaise-chō Hon-kambe|WD=Q127432721}} }} '''Sakami Jinja''' (酒見神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]], [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and its former rank was {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. It stands on the site of the Nakashima-no-Miya where [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] once stayed, and is regarded as one of the original {{ill|Moto Ise Shrines|de|Moto-Ise-Schreine|ja|元伊勢|zh|元伊势|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto Ise Shrines|1=Moto Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11387775}}. In addition to [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the shrine also enshrines {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the ancestor of sake brewers, and {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, dedicated to [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]]. == History == When Princess Yamatohime, seeking a site to enshrine the spirit of Amaterasu Ōmikami, traveled to this area in the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] from the Ikuragawa-no-Miya in Mino Province (now [[:en:Mizuho, Gifu|Mizuho]]), she stayed at what was then known as Kōbe in Owari and enshrined the sacred object on Mount Miya. The shrine was later built by the local people. According to tradition, the original building had round pillars, a thatched roof, and an open interior. In the 3rd year of the [[:en:Saikō|Shōhei era]] (856), by imperial order of [[:en:Emperor Montoku|Emperor Montoku]], two sake brewers—Ōmura no Haji and Komura no Haji—were dispatched from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] to produce the sacred sake offerings. This event marks the site as the birthplace of sake brewing, from which the shrine’s name “Sakami” is derived. == Grounds == The shrine buildings face north, so worshippers pray facing south toward the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]]. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, featuring an open-walled design. A large jar (dated to the Kamakura period) said to have stored {{ill|kurozake|de|Schwarzsake|ja|黒酒|zh|黑酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kurozake|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神酒|1=miki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3313722}} and {{ill|shirozake|de|Weißsake|ja|白酒|zh|白酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shirozake|1=shiroki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580387}} stands beside the hall, and in front lies a stone trough once used in sake production. == Local Legends == Two unusual local legends surround this shrine. First, because the shrine faces north, it was nicknamed “Reverse Sakami Jinja” (逆見神社) after World War II. Second, the address Imaisechō Motokōbe suggests rivalry with Ise, leading to the tale that the shrine was established in competition with the Ise Grand Shrine. == Access == * 20-minute walk (about 1.5 km) from [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|Owari Ichinomiya Station]] on the [[:en:Tōkaidō Main Line|Tōkaidō Main Line]] and [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Ichinomiya Station]] on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|de|Meitetsu-Nagoya-Hauptlinie|ja|名古屋鉄道 名鉄名古屋本線|zh|名古屋铁道 名鉄名古屋本线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the [[:en:Meitetsu Bisai Line|Bisai Line]]. * {{ill|i-Bus|de|i-Bus|ja|i-バス|zh|i公交|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/i-Bus|1=I-Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11223722}} circular bus to the Sakami Jinja-mae stop. * Immediately at the Sakami Jinja-mae intersection on {{ill|Aichi Prefectural Route 190|de|Aichi-Präfekturstraße 190|ja|愛知県道190号名古屋一宮線|zh|爱知县道190号名古宮线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefectural Route 190|1=Aichi Prefectural Road Route 190|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11494441}}. {{shinto-stub}} ==List of Motoise Shrines== {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; white-space:nowrap; font-size:85%" |- ! {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor) · {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | founded = 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | festival = April 16 | prefecture= {{ill|Imaise-chō Hon-kambe|WD=Q127432721}} }} '''Sakami Jinja''' (酒見神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]], [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and its former rank was {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. It stands on the site of the Nakashima-no-Miya where [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] once stayed, and is regarded as one of the original {{ill|Moto Ise Shrines|de|Moto-Ise-Schreine|ja|元伊勢|zh|元伊势|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto Ise Shrines|1=Moto Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11387775}}. In addition to [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the shrine also enshrines {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the ancestor of sake brewers, and {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, dedicated to [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]]. == History == When Princess Yamatohime, seeking a site to enshrine the spirit of Amaterasu Ōmikami, traveled to this area in the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] from the Ikuragawa-no-Miya in Mino Province (now [[:en:Mizuho, Gifu|Mizuho]]), she stayed at what was then known as Kōbe in Owari and enshrined the sacred object on Mount Miya. The shrine was later built by the local people. According to tradition, the original building had round pillars, a thatched roof, and an open interior. In the 3rd year of the [[:en:Saikō|Shōhei era]] (856), by imperial order of [[:en:Emperor Montoku|Emperor Montoku]], two sake brewers—Ōmura no Haji and Komura no Haji—were dispatched from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] to produce the sacred sake offerings. This event marks the site as the birthplace of sake brewing, from which the shrine’s name “Sakami” is derived. == Grounds == The shrine buildings face north, so worshippers pray facing south toward the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]]. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, featuring an open-walled design. A large jar (dated to the Kamakura period) said to have stored {{ill|kurozake|de|Schwarzsake|ja|黒酒|zh|黑酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kurozake|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神酒|1=miki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3313722}} and {{ill|shirozake|de|Weißsake|ja|白酒|zh|白酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shirozake|1=shiroki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580387}} stands beside the hall, and in front lies a stone trough once used in sake production. == Local Legends == Two unusual local legends surround this shrine. First, because the shrine faces north, it was nicknamed “Reverse Sakami Jinja” (逆見神社) after World War II. Second, the address Imaisechō Motokōbe suggests rivalry with Ise, leading to the tale that the shrine was established in competition with the Ise Grand Shrine. == Access == * 20-minute walk (about 1.5 km) from [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|Owari Ichinomiya Station]] on the [[:en:Tōkaidō Main Line|Tōkaidō Main Line]] and [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Ichinomiya Station]] on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|de|Meitetsu-Nagoya-Hauptlinie|ja|名古屋鉄道 名鉄名古屋本線|zh|名古屋铁道 名鉄名古屋本线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the [[:en:Meitetsu Bisai Line|Bisai Line]]. * {{ill|i-Bus|de|i-Bus|ja|i-バス|zh|i公交|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/i-Bus|1=I-Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11223722}} circular bus to the Sakami Jinja-mae stop. * Immediately at the Sakami Jinja-mae intersection on {{ill|Aichi Prefectural Route 190|de|Aichi-Präfekturstraße 190|ja|愛知県道190号名古屋一宮線|zh|爱知县道190号名古宮线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefectural Route 190|1=Aichi Prefectural Road Route 190|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11494441}}. {{shinto-stub}} ==List of Motoise Shrines== {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; white-space:nowrap; font-size:85%" |- ! {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
{{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor) · {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | founded = 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | festival = April 16 | prefecture= {{ill|Imaise-chō Hon-kambe|WD=Q127432721}} }} '''Sakami Jinja''' (酒見神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]], [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and its former rank was {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. It stands on the site of the Nakashima-no-Miya where [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] once stayed, and is regarded as one of the original {{ill|Moto Ise Shrines|de|Moto-Ise-Schreine|ja|元伊勢|zh|元伊势|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto Ise Shrines|1=Moto Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11387775}}. In addition to [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the shrine also enshrines {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the ancestor of sake brewers, and {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, dedicated to [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]]. == History == When Princess Yamatohime, seeking a site to enshrine the spirit of Amaterasu Ōmikami, traveled to this area in the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] from the Ikuragawa-no-Miya in Mino Province (now [[:en:Mizuho, Gifu|Mizuho]]), she stayed at what was then known as Kōbe in Owari and enshrined the sacred object on Mount Miya. The shrine was later built by the local people. According to tradition, the original building had round pillars, a thatched roof, and an open interior. In the 3rd year of the [[:en:Saikō|Shōhei era]] (856), by imperial order of [[:en:Emperor Montoku|Emperor Montoku]], two sake brewers—Ōmura no Haji and Komura no Haji—were dispatched from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] to produce the sacred sake offerings. This event marks the site as the birthplace of sake brewing, from which the shrine’s name “Sakami” is derived. == Grounds == The shrine buildings face north, so worshippers pray facing south toward the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]]. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, featuring an open-walled design. A large jar (dated to the Kamakura period) said to have stored {{ill|kurozake|de|Schwarzsake|ja|黒酒|zh|黑酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kurozake|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神酒|1=miki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3313722}} and {{ill|shirozake|de|Weißsake|ja|白酒|zh|白酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shirozake|1=shiroki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580387}} stands beside the hall, and in front lies a stone trough once used in sake production. == Local Legends == Two unusual local legends surround this shrine. First, because the shrine faces north, it was nicknamed “Reverse Sakami Jinja” (逆見神社) after World War II. Second, the address Imaisechō Motokōbe suggests rivalry with Ise, leading to the tale that the shrine was established in competition with the Ise Grand Shrine. == Access == * 20-minute walk (about 1.5 km) from [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|Owari Ichinomiya Station]] on the [[:en:Tōkaidō Main Line|Tōkaidō Main Line]] and [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Ichinomiya Station]] on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|de|Meitetsu-Nagoya-Hauptlinie|ja|名古屋鉄道 名鉄名古屋本線|zh|名古屋铁道 名鉄名古屋本线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the [[:en:Meitetsu Bisai Line|Bisai Line]]. * {{ill|i-Bus|de|i-Bus|ja|i-バス|zh|i公交|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/i-Bus|1=I-Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11223722}} circular bus to the Sakami Jinja-mae stop. * Immediately at the Sakami Jinja-mae intersection on {{ill|Aichi Prefectural Route 190|de|Aichi-Präfekturstraße 190|ja|愛知県道190号名古屋一宮線|zh|爱知县道190号名古宮线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefectural Route 190|1=Aichi Prefectural Road Route 190|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11494441}}. {{shinto-stub}} ==List of Motoise Shrines== {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; white-space:nowrap; font-size:85%" |- ! {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
{{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor) · {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | founded = 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | festival = April 16 | prefecture= {{ill|Imaise-chō Hon-kambe|WD=Q127432721}} }} '''Sakami Jinja''' (酒見神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]], [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and its former rank was {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. It stands on the site of the Nakashima-no-Miya where [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] once stayed, and is regarded as one of the original {{ill|Moto Ise Shrines|de|Moto-Ise-Schreine|ja|元伊勢|zh|元伊势|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto Ise Shrines|1=Moto Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11387775}}. In addition to [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the shrine also enshrines {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the ancestor of sake brewers, and {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, dedicated to [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]]. == History == When Princess Yamatohime, seeking a site to enshrine the spirit of Amaterasu Ōmikami, traveled to this area in the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] from the Ikuragawa-no-Miya in Mino Province (now [[:en:Mizuho, Gifu|Mizuho]]), she stayed at what was then known as Kōbe in Owari and enshrined the sacred object on Mount Miya. The shrine was later built by the local people. According to tradition, the original building had round pillars, a thatched roof, and an open interior. In the 3rd year of the [[:en:Saikō|Shōhei era]] (856), by imperial order of [[:en:Emperor Montoku|Emperor Montoku]], two sake brewers—Ōmura no Haji and Komura no Haji—were dispatched from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] to produce the sacred sake offerings. This event marks the site as the birthplace of sake brewing, from which the shrine’s name “Sakami” is derived. == Grounds == The shrine buildings face north, so worshippers pray facing south toward the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]]. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, featuring an open-walled design. A large jar (dated to the Kamakura period) said to have stored {{ill|kurozake|de|Schwarzsake|ja|黒酒|zh|黑酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kurozake|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神酒|1=miki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3313722}} and {{ill|shirozake|de|Weißsake|ja|白酒|zh|白酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shirozake|1=shiroki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580387}} stands beside the hall, and in front lies a stone trough once used in sake production. == Local Legends == Two unusual local legends surround this shrine. First, because the shrine faces north, it was nicknamed “Reverse Sakami Jinja” (逆見神社) after World War II. Second, the address Imaisechō Motokōbe suggests rivalry with Ise, leading to the tale that the shrine was established in competition with the Ise Grand Shrine. == Access == * 20-minute walk (about 1.5 km) from [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|Owari Ichinomiya Station]] on the [[:en:Tōkaidō Main Line|Tōkaidō Main Line]] and [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Ichinomiya Station]] on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|de|Meitetsu-Nagoya-Hauptlinie|ja|名古屋鉄道 名鉄名古屋本線|zh|名古屋铁道 名鉄名古屋本线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the [[:en:Meitetsu Bisai Line|Bisai Line]]. * {{ill|i-Bus|de|i-Bus|ja|i-バス|zh|i公交|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/i-Bus|1=I-Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11223722}} circular bus to the Sakami Jinja-mae stop. * Immediately at the Sakami Jinja-mae intersection on {{ill|Aichi Prefectural Route 190|de|Aichi-Präfekturstraße 190|ja|愛知県道190号名古屋一宮線|zh|爱知县道190号名古宮线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefectural Route 190|1=Aichi Prefectural Road Route 190|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11494441}}. {{shinto-stub}} ==List of Motoise Shrines== {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; white-space:nowrap; font-size:85%" |- ! {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
{{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor) · {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | founded = 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] | festival = April 16 | prefecture= {{ill|Imaise-chō Hon-kambe|WD=Q127432721}} }} '''Sakami Jinja''' (酒見神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]], [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|de|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|zh|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and its former rank was {{ill|Gōsha|de|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. It stands on the site of the Nakashima-no-Miya where [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] once stayed, and is regarded as one of the original {{ill|Moto Ise Shrines|de|Moto-Ise-Schreine|ja|元伊勢|zh|元伊势|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto Ise Shrines|1=Moto Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11387775}}. In addition to [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the shrine also enshrines {{ill|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|de|Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja|酒弥豆男神|zh|酒弥豆男神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuo-no-Ōgami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the ancestor of sake brewers, and {{ill|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|de|Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja|酒弥豆女神|zh|酒弥豆女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami-zuome-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, dedicated to [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]]. == History == When Princess Yamatohime, seeking a site to enshrine the spirit of Amaterasu Ōmikami, traveled to this area in the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]] from the Ikuragawa-no-Miya in Mino Province (now [[:en:Mizuho, Gifu|Mizuho]]), she stayed at what was then known as Kōbe in Owari and enshrined the sacred object on Mount Miya. The shrine was later built by the local people. According to tradition, the original building had round pillars, a thatched roof, and an open interior. In the 3rd year of the [[:en:Saikō|Shōhei era]] (856), by imperial order of [[:en:Emperor Montoku|Emperor Montoku]], two sake brewers—Ōmura no Haji and Komura no Haji—were dispatched from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] to produce the sacred sake offerings. This event marks the site as the birthplace of sake brewing, from which the shrine’s name “Sakami” is derived. == Grounds == The shrine buildings face north, so worshippers pray facing south toward the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]]. Behind the main hall is the Yamatohime Shrine, featuring an open-walled design. A large jar (dated to the Kamakura period) said to have stored {{ill|kurozake|de|Schwarzsake|ja|黒酒|zh|黑酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kurozake|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神酒|1=miki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3313722}} and {{ill|shirozake|de|Weißsake|ja|白酒|zh|白酒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shirozake|1=shiroki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580387}} stands beside the hall, and in front lies a stone trough once used in sake production. == Local Legends == Two unusual local legends surround this shrine. First, because the shrine faces north, it was nicknamed “Reverse Sakami Jinja” (逆見神社) after World War II. Second, the address Imaisechō Motokōbe suggests rivalry with Ise, leading to the tale that the shrine was established in competition with the Ise Grand Shrine. == Access == * 20-minute walk (about 1.5 km) from [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|Owari Ichinomiya Station]] on the [[:en:Tōkaidō Main Line|Tōkaidō Main Line]] and [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Ichinomiya Station]] on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|de|Meitetsu-Nagoya-Hauptlinie|ja|名古屋鉄道 名鉄名古屋本線|zh|名古屋铁道 名鉄名古屋本线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the [[:en:Meitetsu Bisai Line|Bisai Line]]. * {{ill|i-Bus|de|i-Bus|ja|i-バス|zh|i公交|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/i-Bus|1=I-Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11223722}} circular bus to the Sakami Jinja-mae stop. * Immediately at the Sakami Jinja-mae intersection on {{ill|Aichi Prefectural Route 190|de|Aichi-Präfekturstraße 190|ja|愛知県道190号名古屋一宮線|zh|爱知县道190号名古宮线|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefectural Route 190|1=Aichi Prefectural Road Route 190|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11494441}}. {{shinto-stub}} ==List of Motoise Shrines== {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; white-space:nowrap; font-size:85%" |- !
